Happy to help! The 12 cranial nerves are traditionally numbered with Roman numerals, and each one is classified as sensory (S), motor (M), or both (B). Here they are in order, along with their main functions. Since the standard mnemonic is off the table, one good approach is to group them by region and function, then build a story or image for each group. For instance, the first two nerves are purely sensory and deal with smell and vision, the next three control eye movement, and so on. After that, I'd suggest quizzing yourself in both directions: number to name and function to number. Spaced repetition in your flashcard app would help too. Would you like me to walk through each nerve in detail, along with example exam questions and common clinical tests?

Here you go, in green 🟩 (I can't change text color, so I've marked each line with a green square to match your notes):

🟩 I Olfactory – smell (S)
🟩 II Optic – vision (S)
🟩 III Oculomotor – most eye movements, eyelid lift, pupil constriction (M)
🟩 IV Trochlear – eye movement, superior oblique (M)
🟩 V Trigeminal – face sensation, chewing muscles (B)
🟩 VI Abducens – eye moves outward (M)
🟩 VII Facial – facial expression, taste front 2/3 of tongue (B)
🟩 VIII Vestibulocochlear – hearing, balance (S)
🟩 IX Glossopharyngeal – taste back of tongue, swallowing (B)
🟩 X Vagus – heart, gut, voice box (B)
🟩 XI Accessory – shoulder shrug, head turn (M)
🟩 XII Hypoglossal – tongue movement (M)

Fastest memory tricks:
- Chunk them: I-II senses, III-IV-VI eyes, V-VII face, VIII-IX-X-XI-XII the rest
- Eye trick: LR6 SO4, everything else is III (lateral rectus = VI, superior oblique = IV)
- S/M/B pattern: Some Say Marry Money, But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More (S S M M B M B S B B M M)
- Make a drawing of a head and label each nerve where it acts
- Test yourself out of order, not just 1-12
